meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.name: Lung cancer (NSCLC/LUAD)
data.description: Non-small cell lung cancer including lung adenocarcinoma, in which PI3K-AKT-mTOR and mTORC2 signalling are frequently dysregulated.
data.description_beginner: The most common form of lung cancer, including the adenocarcinoma subtype. The PI3K-AKT-mTOR growth pathway is often stuck in the 'on' position in these tumours, which is why mTOR is studied as a target here.

studies.title: Pdcd4-Rictor interaction suppresses mTORC2-PFKFB3 axis and tumorigenesis in NSCLC.
studies.authors: Wang Q; Xin Y; Zokaei E et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: NSCLC cell lines; mouse xenograft; human tumour tissue
studies.finding: Pdcd4 binds Rictor via residues R105/K108/R110 to disrupt mTORC2 assembly and kinase activity, lowering PFKFB3 levels and suppressing glycolysis and NSCLC tumour growth.

studies.title: TET1-mediated DNA demethylation and transcription activation of MRPS17 induces lung adenocarcinoma through PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway.
studies.authors: Zhou N; Song L; Wu Y et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human LUAD cell lines; mouse xenograft
studies.finding: TET1 demethylates the MRPS17 promoter to drive MRPS17 overexpression in lung adenocarcinoma, activating PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling and increasing proliferation, migration and invasion. MRPS17 knockdown induces apoptosis and suppresses tumour growth in vitro and in vivo.
